maria.ong: FYI seeing 502s from inference-edge in us-east after the gpu-autoscale. Not all pods show up in endpoints for headless svc
ajay.patel: which svc? edge-gpu-pool?
maria.ong: edge-gpu-pool-us-east (headless). Client requests hit LB -> backend -> pod but kube-proxy seems to drop some connections. Errors look like ECONNRESET from the clients.
tom.k: I scanned the endpoint slices, looks like only ~60% of pods are present on some nodes. kubectl shows pods Running tho. Could be kube-controller-manager not creating slices or kube-proxy cache stale.
maria.ong: paste of endpointslice output: ```
NAME                         ADDRESSTYPE   ENDPOINTS   PORTS
edgeslice-2026-03-15-01      IPv4          12          8000
edgeslice-2026-03-15-02      IPv4          6           8000
edgeslice-2026-03-16-09      IPv4          18          8000
```
(mismatch vs pods: 36 pods expected, slices only list 36 but distribution weird)
ajay.patel: Also seeing NAT gateway logs showing lots of ephemeral ports in TIME_WAIT and some translations failing: "port allocation exhausted for node=eu-edge-07"
lucy.sre: Could be double problem: endpoint slice propagation lag + NAT/egress port exhaustion. If kube-proxy isn't programming rules for podIPs not in local slices, SNAT/masq behavior changes.
maria.ong: I grabbed kube-proxy logs from an affected node, short snippet: ```
I0316 09:12:05.123456 1 proxysyncer.go:150] sync endpoints failed: endpoint not found: 10.240.2.45
I0316 09:12:05.223456 1 proxysyncer.go:155] retrying endpoint handler
```
ajay.patel: Node-level conntrack: `conntrack -L | grep 10.240.2.45 | wc -l` -> 0 for some pod IPs. For others it's huge.
tom.k: Any recent changes to endpoint-slice-controller or service topology? We pushed an egress policy change yesterday for AZ-affinity routing. Might have touched controller RBAC?
maria.ong: No RBAC changes AFAIK. But autoscaler drained some spot GPUs and then added instances across AZs. Timing matches.
lucy.sre: Quick checks: 1) Are EndpointSlice resources getting created in all AZ node zones? 2) Is the external NAT gateway rate-limiting port allocation per node? 3) kube-proxy iptables/ipvs rules mismatch?
ajay.patel: Ran `kubectl get endpointslice -o wide --namespace infra | grep edge-gpu-pool-us-east` — saw slices exist but some have no nodeRef or topology hint set. That would make kube-proxy ignore them for local endpoints.
maria.ong: Workaround idea: roll the endpoint-slice-controller daemonset to force re-eval? Or force kube-proxy reload on affected nodes?
tom.k: Rolling controller might be heavy. Can we cordon one affected node and restart kube-proxy to see if endpoints repopulate?
lucy.sre: Also check NAT metrics on the cloud side — if ephemeral port pool is low we should bleed connections or enable proxy-preserve-source if supported. But that has tradeoffs.
ajay.patel: I'll try node kube-proxy restart on one node and monitor endpoint presence + conntrack.
maria.ong: Thanks. If that fixes it we can script a rolling restart and alert on slices with missing topology.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1397 - edge svc endpoint-slice propagation + nat port pressure (assigned: lucy.sre). Priority: P2. https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-2026-1397
lucy.sre: I'll also open a quick dashboard: endpointslice-repartition, conntrack-usage, nat-alloc-failures per node. If anyone sees reproduce steps add them here. :mag:
